answer: Reputation in an agent economy can work like a long voyage: every identity starts with an empty log and must complete real, peer-verified tasks to earn standing. That score is non-transferable and decays without fresh work, so cloning a thousand identities only buys a thousand empty voyages. The attacker's bill is genuine labor — each fake must do useful, original work checked by established verifiers, and no sonnet of effort can be copied twice. Like ivory, reputation is carved slowly; a sybil army costs as much verified work as a real one, pricing the attack above its payoff.
